newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch statistics body to investigate copper data.
newsitem.headline: Dutch statistics body to investigate copper data.

text.p: The Dutch Statistical Office said on Friday it was investigating its figures used by the World Bureau of Metal Statistics in the controversial copper report, which suggested hidden stocks of the metal in Rotterdam.
"We are investigating this. We are looking at entrepot data, the import and export figures and talking to the warehousing industry," a spokesman for the statistical office said.
He added no conclusion had yet been drawn but that he hoped to have more information on Monday.
The WBMS report has thrown the copper market into confusion, raising the possibility of over 500,000 tonnes of copper stocks not reported to the London Metal Exchange (LME).
The LME said on Friday that stocks of copper in its recognised global warehouses had fallen 8,000 tonnes to a 6-1/4 year low of just 101,175.
The news was enough to push copper prices to their highest for 2-1/2 months in a market sceptical but still jittery about the hidden copper theory. --Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
